Recommended Highlights This Week

1. National Day Parade 2026 – 9 August, National Stadium

2. Lobby Lounge Peranakan Affair: National Day Special – 8–10 August

3. The Line's Baba Nyonya buffet – 6–30 August

4. Sentosa GrillFest – last two weekends before it closes 16 August

5. J65's Flavours of Türkiye buffet – throughout August

6. Hi Stranger – new immersive cocktail bar

7. Majulah Hunt – island-wide treasure hunt concludes 10 August

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Two promotions running at Shangri-La Singapore this week, both tied to the National Day period. The Line, the hotel's long-running regional showcase buffet, turns to Peranakan heritage with returning guest chef Philip Chia, while The Lobby Lounge puts on a special National Day edition of its regular weekend Peranakan buffet, bringing in live hawker pop-ups rather than just a standard spread.

  • The Line – Rediscover the Flavours of Baba Nyonya Cuisine. Guest Chef Philip Chia returns with Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi Asam Goreng and Nyonya Chap Chye. Valid 6–30 August 2026.

  • The Lobby Lounge – A Peranakan Affair: National Day Special. Weekend Peranakan buffet with live hawker pop-ups – Hainanese chicken rice by Chef Yong Jia, Teochew braised duck rice, and Katong laksa by The Original Katong Laksa Janggut Laksa. Saturday 8 August–Monday 10 August, 12:00pm–2:30pm.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

As Singapore's only beachfront resort, Rasa Sentosa leans into its setting with the Rasa Private Beach BBQ – a self-contained grilling experience set up right on the sand, away from the main restaurant crowds.

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (serves 2 adults and 2 children). Available daily across three timeslots: 2:30pm–5:30pm, 5:30pm–8:30pm and 6:30pm–9:30pm. Valid 5 June–31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

J65 has swapped in a new guest-chef theme for August, bringing in cooks from Shangri-La Bosphorus, Istanbul for a Turkish-flavoured take on its usual seafood-forward international buffet – rich, smoky classics rather than the hotel's usual rotation.

  • J65 – Flavours of Türkiye. Guest chefs from Shangri-La Bosphorus, Istanbul. International Seafood Dinner Buffet from $88++ per adult, $44++ per child; Shangri-La Circle members enjoy 20% off. Running throughout August 2026.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

Makan@JEN sits right above Orchard Road, making it one of the more convenient buffet stops for guests already out shopping or sightseeing in the area.

  • Daily lunch and dinner buffet – typically $30–55++ per person depending on the day's spread. 15% off the total bill for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Overall Summary

This is National Day week – the National Day Parade itself falls on Sunday the 9th, back at the National Stadium for the first time in a decade, with a new indoor drone show and the Presidential Gun Salute now visible from Kallang Basin. Guests without a balloted ticket can still catch the atmosphere around the Kallang precinct, or from the Waterfront Promenade F&B market running the same week. On the Shangri-La side, National Day ties into two genuinely good dining picks – a returning Peranakan guest chef at The Line, and a special National Day edition of The Lobby Lounge's weekend buffet with live hawker pop-ups. Also worth flagging: Sentosa GrillFest closes on the 16th, so this is effectively the last full weekend to send guests before it wraps up.

Events & Festivals

National Day Parade 2026

Singapore marks its 61st birthday this week, with the National Day Parade returning to the National Stadium for the first time in ten years. This year's theme is “Majulah Singapura, Go Beyond!”, and the show includes a new indoor drone light show alongside the usual fireworks, military flypasts and cultural performances. For the first time, the Presidential Gun Salute takes place at Kallang Basin, putting part of the ceremony within view of the public outside the stadium.

Event Date: Sunday, 9 August 2026

Location: National Stadium, Kallang

Admission: Free, via public ballot (largely closed by this point)

Best For: Families / National Pride / First-Time Visitors During NDP Season

Concierge Recommendation: Guests without a ticket shouldn't be discouraged – the Stadium Riverside Walk and wider Kallang precinct still carry a strong festival atmosphere, and the fireworks and drone show are visible from several points along the waterfront without needing to be inside the stadium.

Sentosa GrillFest – Closing Soon

Sentosa's beachfront cookout enters its final stretch, with only two more weekends before it wraps up for the year. Still the same format that's made it a strong recommendation all summer – 42 food vendors across five zones, plus Chef's Grill, an eight-course omakase-style dinner served on the sand.

Event Date: Closes 16 August 2026 (remaining Thu–Sun dates)

Time: 4:00pm–10:30pm

Location: Siloso Beach, Sentosa

Best For: Couples / Groups / Food Lovers / Sunset Diners

Concierge Recommendation: This is the last full weekend to point guests toward it before it closes – worth a direct mention rather than waiting for guests to ask.

Restaurants & Bars

Hi Stranger

A new immersive cocktail bar has opened, built around a sensory, slightly theatrical concept – lava-like projected visuals, molten reflections across the bar surfaces, and a suspended stainless-steel installation as the centrepiece. Less about a specific cuisine and more about the overall atmosphere; a good pick for guests after somewhere visually memorable rather than a straightforward cocktail bar.

Best For: Couples / Young Adults / Photography / Something Different

Concierge Recommendation: A strong “last stop of the night” recommendation – the visual concept alone makes it worth the detour, even for guests who've already had dinner elsewhere.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two more picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Candlenut

The world's first Michelin-starred Peranakan restaurant, tucked into Dempsey Hill's greenery. Chef-owner Malcolm Lee built the menu around his mother's and grandmother's cooking, then pushed it further – traditional Peranakan fare with a creative, occasionally Indonesian-leaning twist. The dining room itself is deliberately understated: high ceilings, bamboo lampshades and rattan furniture that let the food do the talking. The tasting menu changes roughly every two months and runs to more than ten courses, many of them one-bite dishes designed to be eaten in a specific way.

Current Promotion: No specific promotion currently advertised.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required for standard bookings; groups larger than 13 should contact the restaurant directly to arrange.

Operating Hours: Lunch daily 12:00pm–3:00pm (last seating 2:30pm); dinner Sun–Thu 6:00pm–10:00pm, Fri–Sat and eve of public holidays 6:00pm–11:00pm

Address: 17A Dempsey Road, Singapore 249676

Website: https://www.comoepicurean.com/restaurants/candlenut/

Signature Dish to Try: Buah Keluak Fried Rice – the dish most closely associated with the restaurant, built around the famously labour-intensive Indonesian black nut.

Concierge Recommendation: A strong special-occasion pick that doesn't feel as formal as its Michelin star might suggest – good for guests who want serious cooking without a stiff atmosphere.

Rang Mahal

One of Singapore's longest-running fine dining restaurants, open on the third floor of Pan Pacific Singapore since 1971. Rang Mahal has stayed consistently well-regarded across five decades by sticking to a fairly simple formula: rich, properly spiced North and South Indian cooking, served in a genuinely upscale room rather than the more casual banana-leaf format guests might expect from Indian dining elsewhere in the city. The wine list runs to more than 280 labels, which is unusual for a restaurant of this cuisine in Singapore.

Current Promotion: Executive Set Lunch (starter, main and dessert) at SGD58++ per person, available Tuesday to Friday.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required for standard bookings; call ahead to confirm, especially for weekend dinners.

Operating Hours: Daily, lunch 12:00pm–2:30pm; dinner 6:30pm–10:00pm

Address: 7 Raffles Boulevard, Pan Pacific Singapore, Level 3, Singapore 039595

Website: https://www.rangmahal.com.sg/

Signature Dish to Try: Tandoori Fondue – an ensemble of tandoor-grilled kebabs served with garlic naan, good for sharing across a table.

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable recommendation for business dinners or a more formal Indian meal – the Executive Set Lunch is also a good value option to mention for guests with meetings nearby.

Hotel & Hospitality News

Capella Hotel Group – Regional GM Appointment

Capella Hotel Group has appointed Christian Westbeld as regional general manager for Southeast Asia, taking on oversight of Capella Singapore alongside Capella Ubud and Capella Hanoi. Westbeld's background spans 25 years across four continents, including F&B and senior management roles at Raffles Hotels & Resorts in Dubai, Beijing and Singapore, followed by senior operations leadership at MGM China. He returned to Raffles Singapore as general manager in 2017 and most recently served as its managing director.

General Manager: Christian Westbeld – regional oversight of Capella Singapore, Capella Ubud and Capella Hanoi

Best For: Luxury Travellers / Sentosa Guests

Transport & Operational Updates

National Day Weekend Crowds

Expect heavy congestion around Kallang from Friday evening through Sunday night. The road closures and crowd control measures around the National Stadium are for National Day Parade rehearsals, security screening and event set-up in the lead-up to the parade, then for the parade itself on the 9th. Separately, the Waterfront Promenade F&B market (7–11 August) will draw its own crowds to the same general area, adding to the congestion.

Downtown Line Night Works

Downtown Line trains continue stopping earlier on Friday nights (last train around 11:30pm) and starting later on Saturday mornings (from 8:30am). This continues until 5 September while engineering works are finished. Free shuttle buses run every 5–10 minutes between 5:00am and 8:30am on Saturday mornings to bridge the gap, connecting Bukit Panjang, Bugis, MacPherson and Expo stations.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Expect a spike in both arrivals and departures around the National Day long weekend. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Sentosa GrillFest Closes 16 August

Next edition will be the last chance to send guests before GrillFest wraps up for the year.

PIE Overnight Closure – 16 August

The same bridge-launching works that closed sections of the PIE near Potong Pasir/Bendemeer on 2 August will recur on 16 August, 12:00am–5:00am. Full details to follow in the relevant edition.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Sentosa GrillFest closes 16 August – flag this clearly to any guest who's been putting off a visit.

  • The Lobby Lounge's Peranakan National Day Special (8–10 August) is a short window – worth proactively mentioning rather than waiting for guests to ask about National Day dining.

  • Expect National Stadium-area road closures and heavy Kallang traffic from Friday evening through Sunday – build in extra transfer time for any guest activities near the Civic District or East Coast that weekend.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day – National Day Atmosphere Without a Ticket

Afternoon: Walk the Stadium Riverside Walk at Kallang to take in the “Go Beyond” lighted display and pre-parade atmosphere.

Evening: Head to the Waterfront Promenade F&B market (running 7–11 August) for dinner with a view, then find a spot along the Kallang waterfront for the fireworks once the parade begins.

Tip: This area gets extremely crowded after 6pm on the 9th itself – advise guests to arrive by 5pm if they want a decent vantage point without a ticket.

Full Day – Dempsey & Civic District

Morning: Start at Dempsey Hill for a relaxed brunch, then browse the antique and lifestyle stores in the area.

Afternoon: Lunch at Candlenut, then walk it off with a visit to the Botanic Gardens next door.

Evening: Head into the Civic District for dinner at Rang Mahal or The Lobby Lounge's Peranakan National Day Special if the dates align, followed by a nightcap at Hi Stranger.

Tip: Dempsey and the Civic District are on opposite sides of town – budget 20–30 minutes by taxi between the afternoon and evening halves.

2 Days – National Day Weekend

Day 1

Morning: Merlion Park and a walk through the Civic District. Afternoon: Gardens by the Bay. Evening: Dinner at Rang Mahal, then an early night ahead of the next day's crowds.

Day 2 – National Day (9 August)

Morning: Sentosa – A Magical Island Adventure and CRYBABY photo stops while the island is relatively quiet. Afternoon: Return to the mainland before Kallang traffic builds. Evening: Waterfront Promenade F&B market and fireworks viewing from the Kallang waterfront.

Tip: Doing Sentosa in the morning and Kallang in the evening avoids the worst of the National Day crowds, since most of the congestion builds later in the day around the stadium.

Quick Reference

Best Free National Day Experience: Stadium Riverside Walk & Waterfront Promenade F&B Market

Best New Bar: Hi Stranger

Best Special-Occasion Dining: Candlenut

Best Business Dinner: Rang Mahal

Best Last-Chance Pick: Sentosa GrillFest (closes 16 August)

Best National Day Dining: The Lobby Lounge's Peranakan National Day Special
